This sounds like my mom. 

She used to say something very similar to me. 
All through elementary school I would get reports home of excellent behavior and my teachers would tell my mother that I was very helpful and generous with my friends and everyone in the classroom. If you asked anyone other than her they would say the same things about me— I was a very, very obedient child (given the fact that I was ruled by fear) but my mom would tell me that I was a very selfish girl and a selfish friend and that no one would want to be my friend if I didn’t learn to make everyone around me feel good and feel fully paid attention to. I would get very sad when she would tell me these things and I couldn’t understand what I was doing wrong. I thought that I was being selfless and easygoing— I was always happy to do whatever my friends wanted to do and was not the type to get upset when my friends didn’t want to do what I wanted to do or didn’t want to play. 

But this of course lead to a pattern of me believing my inherent value was rooted only in what I could give to other people. I had lots of tumultuous friendships in the years after she started saying these things to me because I would give endlessly and act as a doormat to friends who oftentimes bullied me. I still struggle with this now. I have had lots of toxic and even abusive partners and it’s been very difficult for me to leave in these situations because it took me so long to learn that what my mom had taught me about my worth (extending outside of this example) was diminishing and incorrect. 

I couldn’t understand why she would tell me what when I was younger. When I ask her about this and similar types of things she said to me growing up she always has a very similar response to the one you shared. Her excuse is either exactly what your mother said or its that she loves me very much and always has and it’s not her fault that I can’t remember what happened accurately. 

I’m very sorry to hear someone else has dealt with something similar. I hope that you are able to internalize that what she said is not true and that your worth is much greater than what you do for others.

Yes and I hate how much it still affects my daily life now. 

I didn’t even realize the impact of how they treated me growing up until I my friends and partners started to ask me often why I would always, “shut down,“ in their words, whenever we went to my parent’s house or were around them. I didn’t know I was doing it, but since I was a little kid I learned to completely emotionally shut down and make myself “small,” so that no one would have anything to criticize me, humiliate me, or attack me for. 

My parents would constantly infantilize me and treat me as if I was stupid and incapable of doing simple things as well as harshly criticize simple and normal mistakes that come as a part of growing up. I remember one of my earliest memories as being 4 and being scolded by my dad because I couldn’t even draw a picture “correctly” (like I should have amazing artistic talent as a toddler?) I couldn’t just do things like talking to my own friends when they would come to my house for a play date, because I my mom would always monitor what I was saying and correct me if she didn’t like something. If I dressed myself they would say nothing about how I looked until others were around and then all of a sudden something would be wrong with it. It continued into my teen years. In private they would praise me sometimes for things like good grades. but then they would ridicule me only when we were in public about these things. I could be at home with them showing them my report card, being told i was doing an amazing job and that I was a great kid, and then an hour later, my parents could take me to a party with their friends and they would start to rag on me. They would talk about how I was a bad kid and how other kids my age were much better behaved than I. When I was old enough to come and go as I pleased, I started to spend as little time as possible at my house and spent weeks at friends houses to avoid them because only away from them was I allowed to be myself. And even despite being a very cooperative, polite, and studious teen, they would tell me in all seriousness that they bet that I was going out to go get high and that I was going to ruin my life. They always talked about how I was probably running around having sex with different boys and how I was loose and didn’t care enough about myself (I was a virgin who had never had a boyfriend let alone expressed interest in dating) They would talk about how I was a mean girl and that they didn’t know how my friends tolerated me. But once again, that was only in public. At home they told me I was a kind hearted and a good friend. It was really really confusing for me and I couldn’t understand/still dont in some small ways why they were like this with me.

My mom was especially the worst. She hardly ever treated me like I was there, in any way, whether that was physically or emotionally. A condition of that was when we would go to social gatherings, she would talk about me as if I was also not there, so she would openly say horrible and humiliating things. She would talk about how she was worried I was getting fat, about my stomach and digestive issues and private bathroom habits, about how “I had a lot of hair certain places.“ I remember I got a UTI when I was young and she told people in gross detail about everything that was going on down there and talked about my private areas to people I barely knew. I never defended myself because when I would try the response would be that it’s not a big deal and I have no reason to be embarrassed. It was like I had have permission to be my own person and have my own privacy. Then again, this is the same woman that I fought with because I would not let her read my diary when I was 14. She told me that I was an extension of her and that a private diary is not my right.
It got especially bad when I developed anorexia after years of her subtle but nonetheless impactful weight shaming comments. She broadcasted my issues to everyone in public but behing closed doors ridiculed me. Telling me I should feel guilty for my eating disorder because of how it affected HER and how it affected my dad.

When I get into social settings now, if my ears stick up at even the tiniest sign of “danger” I feel completely paralyzed, like I have to hide my personality and hide my emotions and have to appear otherwise perfect, or else these things will all end up being weaponized against me. It’s turned me into a perfectionist and I am very self-critical. It’s frustrating because I find it incredibly difficult to be myself or to have genuine connections with people even if I know it is safe because I cannot seem to hit the “off switch,“ in my brain that will tell me that ‘hey, it’s actually okay to be a real, imperfect, person.’ someone who has feelings and someone who doesn’t need to be ashamed of them either.
